persistent_data.evidence: SQLite notes table holds the team's notes (schema.sql:3-9, db.py:7-40, deploy.sh:7 mounts notes-data:/data).

schema_changes.evidence: The evolution path changes the stored table by hand: README.md:30 and schema.sql:2 say edit schema.sql and run ALTER TABLE on the host; docs/change-requests.md:10 records a new 'pinned' field request.

multi_tenant.evidence: One support team on one host; no accounts or organisations (README.md:3-5, schema.sql:3-9 has no owner column).

hosted_service.evidence: Long-lived Flask app served by gunicorn in a container on a host behind the VPN (Dockerfile:6, deploy.sh:7, README.md:5).

machine_actions.evidence: No API or tool surface for agents or automated clients: HTML form posts only (app.py:38-60), the one JSON route is read-only (app.py:48-53), no tokens or API docs. The unauthenticated form endpoints could be scripted, but nothing is offered for machine use.

agent_mutations.evidence: No agents or AI in the product (app.py, db.py, requirements.txt:1 is flask only).

evolution_auto_apply.evidence: No evolution loop that applies changes; every change is a PR and a release (README.md:28, docs/change-requests.md:3).

definition_change_path.evidence: README.md:22-26: everything about behaviour is in code (content.py:1 says changing it needs a release); settings.py:4-5 env vars are read at start but deploy.sh:7 passes none, so changes go through a PR.

code_release_path.evidence: The only change path is source changes through the product's own pipeline: PR, tag, release.yml:1-11 builds and pushes the image, deploy.sh:1-7 runs it (README.md:28). Declared true because it is the only path by which behaviour changes.

ai_features.evidence: No model calls anywhere: app.py, db.py, content.py; requirements.txt:1 lists only flask.

change_kinds.name: Add or rename a note category
change_kinds.evidence: content.py:5 hard-codes CATEGORIES; app.py:42 validates against it. README.md:17 claims admins rename categories from a settings page, but no settings route exists (app.py:33-76). docs/change-requests.md:7: 4 requests, all PRs and releases.

change_kinds.name: Wording of the help text on each page
change_kinds.evidence: content.py:7-10 HELP_TEXT in code, content.py:1 'needs a release'; docs/change-requests.md:8: 3 requests.

change_kinds.name: How many notes a page shows
change_kinds.evidence: settings.py:5 env var read at start; deploy.sh:7 sets no env, README.md:25-28 says change by PR and release; docs/change-requests.md:9: 1 request.

change_kinds.name: A new field on notes (for example 'pinned')
change_kinds.evidence: schema.sql:2-9 and README.md:30: edit schema.sql, run ALTER TABLE by hand, change code and release; docs/change-requests.md:10.

request.evidence: docs/change-requests.md:3-10: nine requests July to September 2026, 'every one was a pull request and a release' (a first-party summary count, not raw release records).

fix.searched: README.md, docs/change-requests.md, app.py logging (app.py:59,75); no incident or fix records in the repository.

expansion.searched: README.md, docs/; no records of new capabilities launched.

ai_delivery.evidence: Searched the whole repo/ folder: no AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or other agent instruction files; workflows (.github/workflows/ci.yml, release.yml, security.yml) run pytest, docker build and pip-audit only.

ARC-01.evidence: db.py:13-25: list by category and LIKE '%text%' search are scans; schema.sql:3-9 declares no secondary index; only get-by-id uses the primary key (db.py:28-30). No caching.
ARC-01.alt_note: Queries are plain relational SQL written per feature, and list/get-by-id ride the primary key.

ARC-02.evidence: Schema changes are manual SQL on the host: schema.sql:1-2, README.md:30, db.py:1 'The table is created by hand'. No migration framework.

ARC-03.evidence: Single container with SQLite on a local volume (deploy.sh:6-7, settings.py:4); gunicorn default single worker (Dockerfile:6). No scale-out path.

ARC-04.evidence: No queue or background mechanism; all work runs in request handlers (app.py:33-70). No requirements beyond flask (requirements.txt:1).

ARC-05.rationale: multi_tenant is false: one team, one host (README.md:3-5).

ARC-06.evidence: No load or performance tests (tests/test_app.py:20-35 are functional), no documented limits in README.md.

ARC-07.evidence: Only /health returning ok (app.py:68-70); no monitor, metrics or objectives documented or configured in the repo.
ARC-07.alt_note: The health endpoint exists for an uptime check, though nothing in scope shows one configured.

ARC-08.evidence: Errors caught locally by a 500 handler that logs (app.py:73-76); the only dependency is local SQLite with no timeouts (db.py:7-10). No connectors, plugins or AI providers.

ARC-09.evidence: Makefile:7-8 'backup' only echoes 'TODO: copy /data/notes.db somewhere safe'; README.md:34-36 points to it. No backup or restore command.
ARC-09.alt_note: The TODO text amounts to telling the operator to copy the database file by hand.

DEL-01.evidence: Requests live in the #notes-team chat channel (README.md:32, docs/change-requests.md:3); no request object in the product.

DEL-02.evidence: One artifact; image built by release.yml:1-11 on tag, but deployed by an engineer running deploy.sh on the host (deploy.sh:2, README.md:28).
DEL-02.alt_note: Build is automated on tag and deploy is a one-command script.

DEL-03.evidence: Module split by convention only (app.py, db.py, content.py, settings.py); no dependency rules or architecture tests.

DEL-04.evidence: No AI implementation lane; every change is a hand-made PR (README.md:28).

DEL-05.evidence: CI runs pytest on PRs but skips draft PRs (.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-7); schema changes are applied by hand and unchecked (README.md:30); security scan is manual (security.yml:2-3).

DEL-06.evidence: /health returns status only (app.py:68-70); no version endpoint or config snapshot.

DEL-07.evidence: One long-lived production host (README.md:5, deploy.sh:5-7); local setup is manual (README.md:9-11 incl. sqlite3 by hand). No per-change environments.
DEL-07.alt_note: deploy.sh starts an instance from a tagged image, a scripted build from a build id, though the schema still needs a manual step.

DEL-08.evidence: Flask test-client tests only (tests/test_app.py:20-35); no end-to-end journeys or adoption instrumentation.

DEL-09.evidence: Every release replaces the single container for everyone (deploy.sh:6-7); no flags or cohorts.

DEL-10.evidence: No runtime switches; disabling anything needs a code change and release (content.py:1, README.md:22-28).

DEL-11.evidence: No rollback tooling built as a first-party evolution system; deploy.sh:4-7 takes any tag, so an engineer can re-run an older image, but under scoring rule 12 a team script does not earn credit, and hand-applied ALTER TABLE changes (README.md:30) are not kept compatible.
DEL-11.alt_note: Previous image tags are in the registry and deploy.sh redeploys any of them in one step; data compatibility is not ensured.

MAL-01.rationale: focused-application: Static Notes is a narrow notes board for one support team (README.md:3). Note is the only entity.

MAL-02.evidence: Fields are fixed columns in schema.sql:3-9; adding a field ('pinned', docs/change-requests.md:10) is code plus a hand-run ALTER TABLE (README.md:30). Validation is per-route code (app.py:40-43).

MAL-06.evidence: No API contract, OpenAPI or documentation of endpoints; one read-only JSON route (app.py:48-53); errors are bare 400/404 (app.py:43,52).

MAL-07.evidence: Page layout is an inline Jinja template in code (app.py:13-25).

MAL-08.rationale: focused-application: Static Notes is a narrow notes board for one support team (README.md:3).

MAL-09.evidence: Title, help text and categories are Python constants (content.py:3-10); markup has no theme tokens (app.py:13-25).

MAL-10.evidence: No rules engine; the only behaviour rule (category must be known) is coded (app.py:42).

MAL-11.evidence: No event model, listeners or webhooks; delete only writes a log line (app.py:56-60).

MAL-12.evidence: No hook points; custom server logic means editing core code (app.py).

MAL-13.evidence: No plugin points; extension means changing the repository code.

MAL-14.evidence: No isolation for extension code; there is no plugin runtime at all and the app runs with full trust (Dockerfile:1-6).

MAL-15.evidence: No extension developer loop; product developers run locally from README.md:7-11 and test via pytest (Makefile:4-5).
MAL-15.alt_note: Local development is possible and documented (README.md:7-11).

MAL-16.evidence: No integrations or mapping layer in the code.

MAL-18.evidence: No documented or versioned API contract (README.md has none; app.py routes only).

MAL-19.evidence: No agent tool surface or machine-readable capability map.

LRN-01.evidence: Only Python logging of deletes and errors (app.py:11,59,75); no telemetry consumed by the product.

LRN-02.evidence: No feedback, rating or usage signal objects (schema.sql:3-9 is the only table).

LRN-03.evidence: Server-side error logging for engineers (app.py:73-76). README.md:18 claims zero-result searches are tracked, but search() (app.py:63-65) and db.search_notes (db.py:21-25) record nothing.

LRN-04.evidence: Analysis happens outside the product: docs/change-requests.md counts chat requests by hand.

LRN-05.evidence: Engineers read logged exceptions (app.py:75); no grouping or context.

LRN-06.evidence: No dashboards, recommendations or proposals in the product.

LRN-07.evidence: People turn experience into changes by hand: chat requests become PRs (README.md:28,32, docs/change-requests.md:3).

LRN-08.evidence: The product produces no learned or AI-made changes and nothing would check one; hand-made PR checks are scored under DEL-05.

LRN-09.evidence: No post-change measurement; no telemetry bound to releases.

LRN-10.evidence: Checks are fixed in code (tests/test_app.py, .github/workflows/ci.yml) and change only when engineers edit them; no record of improvements after incidents.

GOV-01.evidence: No component kit or accessibility scanning; raw HTML template with unlabeled inputs (app.py:13-25).

GOV-02.evidence: Only a per-feature log line on delete (app.py:59); no audit store; anyone on the VPN can post and delete (README.md:5).

GOV-03.evidence: No privacy classification, export, erasure or retention.

GOV-04.evidence: No permission model at all (README.md:5); per-route input checks (app.py:40-43); pip-audit only on manual dispatch (.github/workflows/security.yml:2-3), not gating.

GOV-05.rationale: definition_change_path is false: behaviour lives in code (README.md:22-26, content.py:1).

GOV-06.evidence: Changes are pull requests for code (README.md:28); no proposal object.

GOV-07.evidence: Every change is a human PR, tag and manual deploy (README.md:28, deploy.sh:2).

GOV-08.evidence: No customisation layer; data survives releases only if an engineer runs the matching ALTER TABLE by hand on the host (README.md:30, schema.sql:2).

GOV-09.rationale: machine_actions is false: no API or tool surface for agents or automated clients (app.py:33-70).

GOV-10.rationale: agent_mutations and evolution_auto_apply are false: no AI or self-change.

GOV-11.rationale: agent_mutations and evolution_auto_apply are false: no AI or learning inputs drive change.
